events.title: The martyrdom of St. Peter Chanel
events.shortBlurb: The Marist whom Futuna called 'the man with the kind heart' became Oceania's first martyr…
body: On 28 April 1841 Pierre Louis Marie Chanel, priest of the Society of Mary, was clubbed to death on the island of Futuna by warriors sent by King Niuliki — the protomartyr of Oceania.

Born in 1803 at Cuet in the diocese of Belley, a shepherd's son, he was ordained in 1827 and revived the derelict parish of Crozet before joining Fr. Jean-Claude Colin's new Marist congregation; professed in September 1836, he sailed that Christmas Eve as superior of the first Marist band to the South Seas, landing on Futuna on 8 November 1837 with Brother Marie-Nizier Delorme.

Three years of hunger, fevers, and slow patience won him the islanders' name of 'the man with the kind heart,' and a few converts; but when the king's own son Meitala sought baptism, Niuliki, fearing the new faith, sent his son-in-law Musumusu to kill the missionary. Within two years nearly the whole island had asked for baptism. Pius XII canonized him on 12 June 1954, and he is honored as the patron of Oceania.
